title: PHP Foundations: Typed Domain Code to a Secure PDO Tracker
description: A beginner PHP course covering runtime tooling, strict types, validation, arrays, functions, exceptions, object models, Composer, PDO, sessions, authorization, web security, and a tested capstone.
prerequisites: Ability to create and save a text file
learningOutcomes: Lint, run, diagnose, and organize typed PHP applications
Use validated input, strict comparisons, arrays, functions, exceptions, classes, and interfaces
Build a secure PDO-backed tracker with transactions, authorization, CSRF protection, and tests

lessons.title: PHP Runtime, Files, and Composer
lessons.summary: Run PHP from the CLI, understand request execution, configure strict types, inspect diagnostics, and use Composer autoloading safely.
objectives: Explain and apply PHP Runtime, Files, and Composer
Verify contracts with lint, runtime, and test evidence

blocks.heading: Core model
blocks.bodyMarkdown: PHP executes server-side scripts per request or from the command line. Begin files with `<?php` and add `declare(strict_types=1);` when building typed application code. Run a script with `php file.php` and use `php -l file.php` for syntax checking. Composer manages packages and generates an autoloader; commit `composer.json` and its lock file for applications, but not the generated vendor directory. Errors should be visible in development and logged without exposing stack traces or secrets to users in production.

blocks.heading: Core model
blocks.bodyMarkdown: PHP supports scalar types, arrays, objects, null, unions, and typed function contracts. Strict types affect scalar argument coercion for calls made from that file; they do not validate external input automatically. Values from command-line arguments, forms, query strings, JSON, and databases remain untrusted. Validate presence, shape, range, and allowed values before constructing domain state. Use `filter_var` only for filters it actually supports, and distinguish missing data from valid zero or empty text. Avoid loose comparisons when types matter.

blocks.heading: Worked PHP example
blocks.bodyMarkdown: Predict types, failures, and output, then lint, run, and compare the evidence.
blocks.codeSource:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);
$text = '19';
$age = filter_var($text, FILTER_VALIDATE_INT);
if ($age === false) { throw new InvalidArgumentException('age'); }
echo ($age + 1) . "\n";

blocks.heading: Core model
blocks.bodyMarkdown: Use `if` chains for ranges and `match` for exact value-to-result mapping. Unlike `switch`, match uses strict comparison, returns a value, and must handle unmatched input. PHP arrays serve as ordered maps and can use integer or string keys. `foreach` can iterate keys and values; avoid reference iteration unless mutation is intentional, and unset the reference afterward to prevent accidental later writes. Functions such as `array_map` and `array_filter` are useful when callbacks remain clear. Test every threshold below, at, and above.

lessons.title: Functions, Exceptions, and Boundaries

blocks.heading: Core model
blocks.bodyMarkdown: Functions should declare parameter and return types and either return domain data or fail according to a documented contract. Default arguments belong after required ones. Nullable types represent valid absence, not generic failure. Throw specific exceptions for violated contracts and catch them at a boundary that can recover, translate, log, or present an error. Do not catch `Throwable` merely to ignore it. Use `finally` only for cleanup that must occur regardless of success. Preserve the previous exception when adding context.

blocks.heading: Worked PHP example
blocks.bodyMarkdown: Predict types, failures, and output, then lint, run, and compare the evidence.
blocks.codeSource:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);
function progress(int $done, int $planned): float {
  if ($done < 0 || $planned <= 0 || $done > $planned) throw new InvalidArgumentException('progress');
  return $done * 100 / $planned;
}
printf("%.1f\n", progress(3, 4));

lessons.title: Classes, Value Objects, and Encapsulation

objectives: Explain and apply Classes, Value Objects, and Encapsulation

blocks.heading: Core model
blocks.bodyMarkdown: A class combines state and behavior. Keep properties private when arbitrary assignment could violate invariants, and validate constructor input before the object becomes observable. Readonly properties can be initialized once and support value objects, but nested referenced objects may still be mutable. Interfaces describe behavior required by consumers; avoid large interfaces that force unrelated methods. Namespaces prevent collisions and map naturally to Composer PSR-4 autoloading. Inject collaborators rather than constructing infrastructure inside domain methods.

blocks.heading: Worked PHP example
blocks.bodyMarkdown: Predict types, failures, and output, then lint, run, and compare the evidence.
blocks.codeSource:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);
final class Progress {
  public function __construct(private int $percent) { if ($percent < 0 || $percent > 100) throw new InvalidArgumentException('percent'); }
  public function percent(): int { return $this->percent; }
}
echo (new Progress(75))->percent() . "\n";

lessons.title: PDO, Sessions, Security, and a Progress Tracker
lessons.summary: Combine PDO transactions, parameterized SQL, sessions, output escaping, CSRF protection, authorization, and tests in a secure tracker.
objectives: Explain and apply PDO, Sessions, Security, and a Progress Tracker
Verify contracts with lint, runtime, and test evidence

blocks.heading: Core model
blocks.bodyMarkdown: Use PDO prepared statements with bound values instead of concatenating SQL, and wrap multi-step writes in a transaction that rolls back on failure. Authentication identifies a user; authorization checks whether that user may access the specific record. Regenerate session identifiers after login and configure secure, HttpOnly, and appropriate SameSite cookies. Escape untrusted text for its output context, usually with `htmlspecialchars` for HTML text. State-changing browser requests need CSRF protection. Store password hashes from `password_hash`, never plaintext passwords, and verify with `password_verify`.

finalAssessment.title: Secure PDO Learning Progress Tracker
finalAssessment.instructionsMarkdown: Build a typed PHP progress tracker using validated domain objects, Composer autoloading, PDO prepared statements and transactions, authenticated record ownership, CSRF-protected mutations, contextual output escaping, secure sessions, and at least ten automated tests.
deliverables: Normal, authorization, validation, and transaction test results
